entry.title: Bolmo’s architecture unlocks efficient byte‑level LM training without sacrificing quality
entry.summary:
Enterprises that want tokenizer-free multilingual models are increasingly turning to byte-level language models to reduce brittleness in noisy or low-resource text. To tap into that niche — and make it practical at scale — the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) introduced Bolmo, a new family of models that leverage its Olmo 3 models by “bytefiying” them and reusing their backbone and capabilities. The company launched two versions, Bolmo 7B and Bolmo 1B, which are “the first fully open byte-level language model,” according to Ai2. The company said the two models performed competitively with — and in some cases surpassed — other byte-level and character-based models.
